name: Enzalutamide (mCRPC)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Enzalutamide is an androgen-receptor inhibitor and is not biomarker-restricted. Castrate testosterone (below 50 ng/dL) must be maintained with ongoing ADT. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Prostate Cancer, Systemic Therapy for M1 CRPC (PROS-18) and PROS-G.

supportiveCare: continue ADT to maintain castrate testosterone below 50 ng/dL (PROS-G).
cycles null: continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
no companion corticosteroid is required with enzalutamide.
monitoring: PSA and serum testosterone (confirm castrate level)

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3 or higher toxicity or seizure
doseModificationRules.text: Hold enzalutamide per labeling; on recovery resume at a reduced dose; discontinue if a seizure occurs; obtain clinical review.

drugs.name: Enzalutamide
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Prostate v6.2026 Discussion (prostate lines 7290, 6880, 6467). Enzalutamide 160 mg PO once daily continuously. No companion steroid required (unlike abiraterone).

provenance.locator: Discussion, prostate line 7290 (enzalutamide 160 mg daily, phase 3 randomized trial); prostate lines 6880 and 6467 (enzalutamide 160 mg/day)
